<!-- pr-reviewer: d11e4375d86bbf65a0fc69bb21d7945c95d3d1e2 -->
Reviewed head d11e4375d86bbf65a0fc69bb21d7945c95d3d1e2. Result: clean.

The fix is correct and it is the smallest shape that removes the race.
`tracing` caches the interest of a callsite for the whole process. The test
installs a thread-local subscriber with `with_default`. Another thread can
hit the same callsite first and cache "never". The lib test binary starts
other threads that emit `diag` lines. In a binary of its own, no other
thread uses these callsites. One test per binary is the law; the file
header says so.

Reads:
- `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`: the race test is out of the lib. The pointer
  comment names the new binary. `the_macros_take_println_shaped_arguments`
  stays and compiles the macros. It emits with no subscriber; that is
  harmless.
- `crates/ui/tests/diag_events.rs`: same asserts as the old test, through
  `diag::warn` / `diag::info`. `tracing` is a dependency and
  `tracing-subscriber` a dev-dependency of `camcraft-ui`; both reach an
  integration binary. `#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` is right.
- `docs/decisions/2595-diag-events-own-binary.md`: the why, the three
  dropped options and the cost match the change.

Gate, run here on the trial-merge with main (011c91397-style merge commit,
trial-merge b08315bf0, parents d11e4375d + a8d923108, clean):
- `diag_events`: 1 passed, 0 failed, run 4 times, no flake.
- `camcraft-ui --lib`: 1247 passed, 4 failed. The 4 fails are exactly the
  known red of main (issue #2762, frame_cost tests). This PR does not
  touch them.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Notes, non-blocking:
- A second test added to `diag_events.rs` brings the race back. The header
  warns about it. Good.
- #2595 has two priority labels (P3 and P5) and two effort labels. The
  maintainer must decide. That is not a blocker for this PR.

Laws: test location is right (ui event tests in `crates/ui/tests/`); file
under 400 lines; no new dependency; no UI change, no screenshot needed.
This PR is test-only. Outside PR: the maintainer approves and merges by
hand.
